chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Ubayd ibn Ziyad: 'The manifestation of the bounty is more beloved to Allah than its maintenance, so beware that you should not be outfitting except in the best of outfits of your people.'
He said, 'So Ubayd was not seen except in the best of outfits of his people until he died.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq teach about displaying God's bounty through clothing?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises Ubayd ibn Ziyad that manifesting God's bounty through dignified appearance is more beloved than merely preserving it, emphasizing the importance of social conformity in attire. This guidance highlights the Shia scholarly view that modesty and beauty are not contradictory, but rather that one should adorn oneself in the finest manner appropriate to one's community to reflect divine grace. The report concludes by noting Ubayd’s consistent adherence to this advice, wearing the best clothes until his death.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Aslam, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Bureyd Bin Muawiya who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to Ubeyd Bin Ziiyad: ‘Manifestation of the Bounty is more beloved to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> than its maintenance, so beware that you should not be outfitting except in the best of outfits of your people’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So Ubdeyd was not seen except in the best of outfits of his people until he died’.
en.sarwar: 15. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Aslam from Harun ibn Muslim from Burayd ibn Mu‘awiyah who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to ‘Ubayd ibn Ziyad, ‘Showing the bounty is more beloved to Allah than its safekeeping. Therefore, you must live in your people with the best dress among them.’
He (the narrator) has said that ‘Ubayd was never seen except with the best dress among his people until he died.’”
